html:
Coffee became Costa Rica's main crop and export from the 1820s, grown in the volcanic soils of the Central Valley around San José. It made a poor colonial backwater into a prosperous republic.

The government gave land to anyone who would plant coffee, so many small and middle farmers grew it alongside the great estates. Ox carts carried the beans to the Pacific port of Puntarenas, and from the 1840s ships took them to Britain. A coffee elite of processors and exporters came to dominate politics.

Coffee money paid for the National Theatre in San José, built in the 1890s, and the trade needed the railway to the Caribbean built by Minor Keith. It shaped the country's pattern of small owners. The story follows the spread of coffee across the tropics, from Yemen to Brazil, and made Costa Rica the first coffee republic of Central America.
sum: Coffee became Costa Rica's main crop and export from the 1820s, grown in the volcanic soils of the Central Valley around San José. It made a poor colonial backwater into a prosperous republic.
